articles.body: Epic's sandbox, an integration platform's dev environment, and the JSON fixtures in your repo. Pick any patient out of Open Epic's sandbox. Camila Lopez, say. Query her today: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN " \ "https://fhir.epic.com/interconnect-fhir-oauth/api/FHIR/R4/Patient/erXuFYUfucBZaryVksYEcMg3" Now query her again next month. Next year. articles.title: I put Gopher on Nostr. Now every npub is a gopherhole
articles.excerpt: TL;DR I've built GopherKind, a publisher and reader for gopherholes stored as signed Nostr events. Every Nostr public key already works as a hole. GopherKind turns the account's profile, notes, replie…
articles.body: TL;DR I've built GopherKind , a publisher and reader for gopherholes stored as signed Nostr events. Every Nostr public key already works as a hole. GopherKind turns the account's profile, notes, replies, long-form articles, and the follows and followers visible through its relays into ordinary Gopher menus and text. An author can then publish proper path-addressed pages as kind 31436 events, and those pages take over the same hole. The same content is readable through Gopher, Gemini, the web and a terminal. Reading needs no account. The CLI publisher uses a NIP-46 remote signer, and GopherKind refuses raw secret keys completely.

articles.body: Honestly, the most humbling thing about building… is the gap between the vision in your head and the potholes you don't see coming. I had this whole picture of where I wanted my skills to go. Clean, production grade, the kind of thing another builder could actually lean on. I would get to a point where I feel good about it, and then something small and dumb would break and send me right back to the start. The one that got me the worst was my skill validator. articles.title: Agentic AI in German: The Words, the Law, the Numbers
articles.excerpt: German does not have a word for agentic, and the workaround the industry settled on is a bad one. "Agentisch" exists as a loan translation and appears in analyst reports, but nobody says it out loud i…
articles.body: German does not have a word for agentic, and the workaround the industry settled on is a bad one. "Agentisch" exists as a loan translation and appears in analyst reports, but nobody says it out loud in a meeting. What people actually say is KI-Agent, which means AI agent, the noun. So the German conversation collapses the adjective into the object, and a distinction that is load-bearing in English quietly disappears. In English you can say a system is somewhat agentic. In German you either have a KI-Agent or you do not, and that binary is a genuinely bad fit for a technology that is a spectrum. I bring this up because it is not a language-nerd observation. It shows up in procurement.
articles.author: Matthias | StudioMeyer

Wada opened up about the Persona studio's development pipeline during an interview with GamerBraves . More than two years removed from the launch of Persona 3 Reload and on the cusp of the release of Persona 4 Revival , fans naturally have one question on their minds: Where are the Persona 1 and 2 remakes? Both games – which actually released in the '90s as Revelations: Persona and Persona 2: Innocent Sin/Eternal Punishment – have, so far, been left out of Atlus' trend of remakes. There's been no word on whether modern-day reimaginings for the two JRPGs will be in the works.

If that interests you, even without context, then you probably have a lot to look forward to. Fields of Mistria is the type of farming sim I wish I had in my youth – it resembles early 2000s cozy classics from Harvest Moon to Animal Crossing, all mixed together into an anime-coded concoction. The world of Mistria is brimming with lore and its villagers have distinct personalities that shine through in their dialogue. I can tell I still have a while before I’ve seen everything its newly released 1.0 update has to offer, but I already can’t wait to learn more about my new home and neighbors.

articles.excerpt: Andromeda has slowed its star-forming rate over the last 40 million years. Scientists think they finally know why.
articles.body: Thanks to the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have shed light on a recent chapter in the history of our Milky Way's neighboring galaxy, Andromeda. Using Hubble Space Telescope observations of Andromeda 's stars, a research team showed that the spiral galaxy's rate of making new stars has dramatically slowed down in the last 40 million years. And they've found more evidence that one of Andromeda's own neighbors — a smaller galaxy called M32 — may be to blame. "We can't explicitly say that we are seeing a decrease in star formation because of M32. But it's right there, and it's definitely the most likely suspect," said Tobin Wainer, a graduate student at the University of Washington and one of the astronomers, in a statement .

articles.title: Lego Project Hail Mary review: Amaze, amaze, amaze!
articles.excerpt: Is the new Lego Project Hail Mary set worth the space on your shelf? We built the movie-inspired set to help you decide if it belongs in your collection.
articles.body: Given how much I enjoyed the Project Hail Mary movie , I was beyond hyped to get my hands on the Lego Project Hail Mary set. And now that I've built it, I'm thrilled to say it does not disappoint. You could even say that it's amaze, amaze, amaze! The titular Hail Mary is the spaceship from "Project Hail Mary", the Andy Weir novel-turned-Hollywood blockbuster that carries Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) across the stars to save humanity. While the design of the ship is certainly described in the book , this is definitely a Lego rendition of the movie version. So, if you're an Andy Weir fan who imagined it looking a little different, you can blame the studio. Coming in at $99.99 with just under 900 pieces, it's a lot smaller than we expected (and hoped for).

articles.title: Chinese rocket explodes less than 90 seconds after liftoff (photos)
articles.excerpt: China's latest rocket launch ended in failure this morning (Aug. 10), lighting up the skies with some unwanted fireworks.
articles.body: China's latest rocket launch ended in failure this morning, lighting up the skies with some unwanted fireworks. The state-owned China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) launched a Long March 7A rocket today (Aug. 10) from the Wenchang Space Launch Site, in the country's Hainan province, just after 8:00 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT; 8:02 p.m. local time). Around 85 seconds into the launch, the rocket exploded, generating a massive fireball and a cloud of smoke and debris while still soaring through Earth's atmosphere . CASC had not yet released a statement about the incident by the time of this story's publication, but video reposted to social media captured the shock of onlookers the moment that the rocket burst into flames.
